# Gronw Pebr: the stories first, then the spelling

You cannot weigh an accent without knowing what it carries. Here is what **Gronw Pebr** has been carrying.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Flower-Wife’s Plot.** Blodeuwedd, made of flowers by Gwydion and Math for the cursed Lleu, met Gronw by the Cynfael and loved him.  Her husband’s invulnerability had one precise condition — he could be killed only while standing with one foot on a bath and one on a goat-skin, and only by a spear worked a year at the dark of the moon.  She persuaded Lleu to demonstrate the posture; Gronw waited behind the bath-house wall with the finished spear.

**The Cast Through the Wall.** The cast went through the wall and through Lleu, who changed into an eagle and vanished into the forest.  Gronw took Blodeuwedd and Lleu’s lands.  But Lleu was found, healed by Gwydion’s wizardry, and returned in a year’s turning — the cursed hero restored by the uncle whose flower-magic had made the wife who betrayed him.

**The Stone of the Return-Cast.** The law of the tale is exact symmetry.  Gronw offered compensation — land, gold, any price — and Lleu refused all but one thing: the return-cast.  Gronw’s single plea was granted: a stone between him and the spear.

## The Name Travels

Gronw is the Welsh cousin of the Indo-European adulter-killer pattern — the lover who strikes the unkillable hero at his one vulnerable posture — but the Mabinogi’s telling is its own: the magic is legalistic, the justice symmetrical, and the villain allowed his one dignified plea.  The flower-wife Blodeuwedd’s fate (changed into an owl, shunned by the other birds) outshines his in later retellings; his stone keeps his share.
